question:
We are planning a project that depends on a third-party API nobody on the team has used and on a performance target we may not be able to reach. How should we handle these things that could go wrong, both when planning the work and while it is under way?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

When a project depends on an unfamiliar third-party API or faces uncertain performance targets, teams should systematically identify and analyze these risks upfront, build mitigation strategies into the plan, and continue monitoring risk throughout the project lifecycle—using prototypes, simulations, and regular reviews to detect problems early and trigger corrective action when thresholds are exceeded.

# Guidelines

- Identify risk factors, analyze the probability and potential impact of each, prioritize them, and develop [SWEBOK excerpt 865049d7f34c4858ec74] minimize [SWEBOK excerpt 1400cd0d41734de0e233]; capture this in a risk register. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Risk Management_ Identification, Analysis, and Mitigation Strategies.md)

- Use risk assessment methods such as [SWEBOK excerpt bb228fe333a5104c91f2] to identify and evaluate risk factors; pay particular attention to risks related to software quality requirements. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Risk Assessment Methods and Software Project Risk Management.md)

- Apply a risk-driven approach to architecture: do just enough software architecture to mitigate identified risks, including those arising from extremely demanding quality requirements or a small solution space. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Architecture_ Foundations, Methods, and Modern Practice/Risk-Driven Software Architecture Approach.md)

- Use simulation and prototyping as [SWEBOK excerpt 7c3169b7ed8bc0826c9e]—to predict behavior and validate performance instead of relying entirely on testing. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Quality Evaluation and Assessment/Design Analysis and Quality Metrics/Formal Analysis and Dynamic Evaluation Techniques.md)

- Use prototyping to explore the least-understood software aspects or components first, since [SWEBOK excerpt 25fa8a35093e44cc5068]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Formal Methods, Agile Development, and Software Quality/Verification and Prototyping Approaches/Prototyping Methods in Software Engineering.md)

- Assess risk, legality, and suitability when acquiring third-party components; verify that each acquired component is complete, correct, and consistent with the architectural design and software requirements. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Supplier Contract Management.md)

- Conduct system functional or preliminary design reviews to ensure the system can proceed into design with acceptable risk and that all functional performance requirements are defined and consistent with budget, schedule, risk, and other constraints. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Quality Assurance Reviews and Implementation Practices/Technical Reviews and Audits in Project Management.md)

- Perform risk management [SWEBOK excerpt 3f32cf09481746d60739]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Continuous Risk and Quality Management/Risk Management Throughout Project Life Cycle.md)

- Use risk management tools—including simulation or decision trees to analyze costs versus payoffs and subjective estimates of probabilities—and Monte Carlo simulation [SWEBOK excerpt 36f2adef4075152e9d58]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Data Collection, Quality Assurance, and Project Monitoring/Project Tracking and Risk Management Tools.md)

- Continually monitor adherence to the project plan; revisit the project risk profile and evaluate adherence to software quality requirements at predetermined intervals, analyzing effort expenditure, schedule adherence, costs, and resource use. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Data Acquisition and Project Measurement/Implementation and Monitoring of Software Project Measurement.md)

- Recalculate risk exposures regularly; identify problems and exceptions based on thresholds that have been exceeded and report outcomes when those thresholds are crossed. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Risk Exposure Recalculation and Threshold Monitoring.md)

- When risk probability and impact are understood, make changes [SWEBOK excerpt 9f048249abfc1c897d24] such as retesting certain software components. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Project Monitoring and Risk-Based Decision Making.md)

- If unanticipated events occur, consider incorporating additional actions (e.g., prototyping to assist in requirements validation) or revising the project plan; document and communicate all decisions to relevant parties and revise plans when necessary. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Software Project Control and Configuration Management.md)

- Ensure requirements are feasible—meaning [SWEBOK excerpt 1f1c1333967b74fab0f5]—and treat performance targets as testable (quantified) requirements so compliance or noncompliance can be clearly demonstrated. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Requirements_ Foundations and Engineering Practices/Requirements Engineering_ Elicitation, Analysis, and Specification/Requirements Analysis and Refinement/Software Requirements Properties and Quality Criteria.md)

- Support all project decisions with realistic process and product estimations and measurements; [SWEBOK excerpt 12c0b524e57fae82ab87], reflect on the overall approach, since inaccurate estimations can cause project failure. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Process Foundations and Measurement/Accuracy in Project Estimations and Measurements.md)
